A student sets a short timer, works in a library or with a friend, and writes just a messy first paragraph. Lowering the bar for starting removes the dread, and momentum usually does the rest.

A child drums fingers or fidgets from boredom, energy or focus. Watching for context, since fidgeting may help concentration, prevents unfair scolding.

A child declares that there is nothing to do and clings to a parent. Boredom is a signal that the mind wants to generate its own activity, but the child does not yet know how.

rows.description: A student admitted to a prestigious institute believes they got in by luck and that everyone will soon find out; success is discounted while comparison with others is harsh.

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: A fresh graduate joins a company and sees confident colleagues using unfamiliar terms. The excitement of being hired mixes with the worry that the selection was a mistake.

A teenager who avoided one presentation begins to dodge group chats, outings and answering the phone. The circle of safe activities shrinks and the world feels more threatening.
